title: Atractylodes macrocephala compounds attenuate pediatric epilepsy neuroinflammation through multitarget regulation of the NF-kappaB pathway.
authors: Cai, Aiyuan; Liu, Ran; Li, Zilong; Huang, Hailong; Xiao, Jing; Lin, Yuanhong; Wu, Haixia; Liu, Ping; Ying, Jing; Hu, Qingpeng
one_liner_zh: 研究白术成分通过NF-kappaB通路缓解小儿癫痫神经炎症，分子对接仅用于药物-蛋白结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: This study investigates the multi-target mechanisms of Atractylodes macrocephala (AM) and its main active component, Atractylenolide III (ATR-III), in mitigating central nervous system (CNS) inflammatory responses in pediatric epilepsy via modulation of the nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-kappaB) signaling pathway. Network pharmacology identified AM's active components and their targets, which were integrated with pediatric epilepsy-related targets. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses revealed potential mechanisms, while molecular docking assessed the binding capacity of ATR-III to key targets. In vitro, an LPS-induced microglial inflammation model was used, with CCK-8 assays, Western blot, qPCR, and JC-1 staining evaluating ATR-III's effects on cell viability, NF-kappaB activation, inflammatory cytokine expression, and mitochondrial function. Network pharmacology showed AM's targets overlap with pediatric epilepsy targets, enriched in neuroinflammation pathways. Molecular docking confirmed ATR-III's strong binding to NF-kappaB targets. In vitro, ATR-III significantly suppressed NF-kappaB activation, reduced p65 and IkappaBalpha phosphorylation, decreased inflammatory cytokines, and improved LPS-induced mitochondrial dysfunction by restoring membrane potential and upregulating PGC-1alpha and COX4. This study elucidates AM and ATR-III's mechanisms in reducing CNS inflammation and improving mitochondrial function, offering a theoretical basis for AM's use in pediatric epilepsy and highlighting ATR-III's potential as a natural anti-inflammatory drug.
abstract_zh: 本研究探讨了白术（Atractylodes macrocephala, AM）及其主要活性成分白术内酯III（Atractylenolide III, ATR-III）通过调节核因子kappa-B（NF-kappaB）信号通路，缓解儿童癫痫中枢神经系统（CNS）炎症反应的多靶点机制。通过网络药理学鉴定了AM的活性成分及其靶点，并与儿童癫痫相关靶点进行整合。基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）分析揭示了潜在机制，而分子对接评估了ATR-III与关键靶点的结合能力。在体外实验中，采用脂多糖（LPS）诱导的小胶质细胞炎症模型，通过CCK-8实验、Western blot、qPCR和JC-1染色评估ATR-III对细胞活力、NF-kappaB激活、炎症细胞因子表达及线粒体功能的影响。网络药理学显示，AM的靶点与儿童癫痫靶点存在重叠，并富集于神经炎症通路。分子对接证实ATR-III与NF-kappaB靶点具有强结合能力。在体外实验中，ATR-III显著抑制NF-kappaB激活，降低p65和IkappaBalpha磷酸化水平，减少炎症细胞因子表达，并通过恢复膜电位和上调PGC-1alpha及COX4改善LPS诱导的线粒体功能障碍。本研究阐明了AM和ATR-III在减轻CNS炎症及改善线粒体功能方面的机制，为AM在儿童癫痫中的应用提供了理论基础，并凸显了ATR-III作为天然抗炎药物的潜力。
